Name: Yaji (West African Suya Spice Rub)
Short description: The dry suya spice rub behind Ghana and Nigeria's chinchinga and suya skewers.
Description: Yaji is the dry rub at the heart of West African suya and chinchinga: grains of selim, dried chillies, crushed kuli-kuli (peanut puffs), ginger powder, a crumbled stock cube, salt, and black pepper. Rub generously onto skewered meat before grilling. Featured in Episode 1 of the Fudi People spice journey series. Dry blend, shelf-stable. Contains peanuts (kuli-kuli); may contain gluten depending on the stock cube used.

Name: Yassa Marinade (Senegal)
Short description: Senegal's sour, mustard-forward marinade behind poulet yassa.
Description: A wet marinade, not a dry blend: mustard paste, onions, garlic, and a real hit of sourness from lemon juice or vinegar, used on chicken or fish before slow-cooking with caramelised onions. Featured in Episode 2. WET, needs adaptation: sold fresh/refrigerated, or reformulated with a shelf-stable acid and dried aromatics, before it can be listed as a pantry product as scripted. Contains mustard.

Name: Niter Kibbeh (Ethiopian Spiced Butter)
Short description: Ethiopia's spiced clarified butter, the base of doro wat.
Description: Butter simmered for 20 minutes with onion, garlic, ginger, fenugreek, cumin, korarima (or cardamom), turmeric, oregano, basil, and sage, then strained through muslin. Featured in Episode 3. WET, needs adaptation: a dairy product needing refrigeration and a limited shelf life, not a dry pantry item as scripted. Contains dairy.
Tags: Horn of Africa,Ethiopia,Wet - Needs Adaptation,Contains Dairy

Name: Pepper Soup Spice (Sierra Leone & Liberia)
Short description: The aromatic base of Sierra Leonean and Liberian pepper soup.
Description: Built from Scotch bonnet peppers, garlic, ginger, country onion (a small wild onion), and often uda and calabash nutmeg, simmered with goat, fish, or chicken. Featured in Episode 4. WET, needs adaptation: the fresh chilli, garlic, ginger, and onion base isn't a dry pantry mix as scripted; a dry version would need to drop the fresh aromatics and sell just the dried spices (uda, calabash nutmeg). Sourced from general research rather than the book, worth double-checking before finalising.

Name: Harissa (Maghreb Chilli Paste)
Short description: The North African chilli paste behind Maghreb cooking.
Description: Dried red chillies (Baklouti if available), soaked and blended with garlic, salt, lemon juice, ground cumin, ground coriander, ground caraway, and olive oil into a paste. Featured in Episode 5. WET, needs adaptation: a chilli paste, not a dry blend; sold as a refrigerated jarred paste rather than a shelf-stable dry mix as scripted.

Name: Pilau Masala (Zanzibar/East Africa)
Short description: Zanzibar's warming pilau spice: cumin, pepper, clove, cardamom, and cinnamon.
Description: Toasted and ground cumin seeds, black peppercorns, cloves, cardamom seeds, and cinnamon, stirred into onions at the start of cooking pilau rice. Featured in Episode 6. Dry blend, shelf-stable. No exact ratios given in the source; test-cook to lock in your own before scaling for retail.

Name: Mbongo Mix (Central Africa)
Short description: Central Africa's smoky mbongo spice base, ground with garlic and onion.
Description: Whole mbongo spice (or black cardamom), bobimbi (or wild garlic), njangsa seeds (or unsalted peanuts), calabash nutmeg (or regular nutmeg), grains of paradise, and garlic cloves, ground together with chopped onion. Featured in Episode 7. WET, needs adaptation: ground with fresh garlic and onion, this comes out a moist paste rather than a dry rub as scripted; a dry version would need onion and garlic powder substituted in. May contain peanuts if using the peanut substitute for njangsa.
Tags: Central Africa,Cameroon,Wet - Needs Adaptation,May Contain Peanuts

Name: Durban Curry Masala (Southern Africa)
Short description: Durban's South Asia-bridge curry masala: coriander, cumin, cardamom, and chilli.
Description: Toasted and ground coriander seeds, cumin seeds, cardamom seeds, fenugreek seeds, cloves, a cinnamon stick, mild chilli powder, and cayenne pepper, with ground ginger stirred through. Featured in Episode 8, the direct bridge into the South Asia sub-arc. Dry blend, shelf-stable. No exact ratios given in the source; test-cook before locking a retail recipe.

Name: Jamaican Jerk Rub (The Caribbean)
Short description: The allspice-and-Scotch-bonnet dry rub behind Jamaican jerk.
Description: Ground allspice, whole black peppercorns, and cloves, combined with chipotle or cayenne powder, paprika, grated nutmeg, ground ginger, ground cinnamon, onion powder, garlic powder, dried thyme, brown sugar, and sea salt. Rub onto chicken, fish, pork, or beef before marinating. Featured in Episode 9, opening the Americas sub-arc. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities straight from the source.

Name: Za'atar (Syria)
Short description: The toasted cumin, sesame, sumac, and oregano blend behind Syrian za'atar.
Description: Cumin seeds dry-roasted with sea salt and ground, combined with dry-roasted sesame seeds, dried oregano, and sumac. Used as a dip with olive oil and bread, or as a seasoning. Featured in Episode 10, opening the Middle East sub-arc. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source. Contains sesame.

Name: Turkish Baharat (Turkey)
Short description: Turkey's warming all-purpose spice blend: pepper, cumin, coriander, and mint.
Description: Ground black peppercorns, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, cloves, cardamom seeds, and nutmeg, with a pinch of cinnamon and dried mint stirred in. Makes roughly 9 tbsp. Featured in Episode 11. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source.

Name: Zhug (Israel)
Short description: Israel's bright, fiery green chilli-herb condiment.
Description: Roasted and ground cardamom, coriander, and cumin seeds, pounded to a paste with fresh green chillies and garlic, then combined with fresh coriander, parsley, olive oil, salt, pepper, and lemon juice. Featured in Episode 12. WET, needs adaptation: a fresh herb paste with a short shelf life, sold fresh/refrigerated rather than as a pantry jar.

Name: Taklia (Lebanon)
Short description: Lebanon's fried-garlic-and-coriander base, the seven-spice baharat's finishing touch.
Description: Garlic cloves gently fried in olive oil until fragrant, then ground with ground coriander, a pinch of cayenne, and sea salt. Featured in Episode 13. WET, needs adaptation: an oil-based fried-garlic paste, not a dry blend; would need reformulating with dried or fried garlic granules and no oil to sell as a shelf-stable product.

Name: Arabic Baharat (Iraq)
Short description: Iraq's all-purpose baharat: pepper, allspice, clove, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Description: Ground black peppercorns, allspice, cloves, coriander seeds, and cumin seeds, combined with cinnamon and grated nutmeg. A genuinely flexible all-purpose rub, marinade base, or seasoning. Featured in Episode 14, the key thread into the South Asia sub-arc. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source.

Name: Advieh (Iran)
Short description: Iran's rose-petal-and-warm-spice blend.
Description: Ground dried rose petals, cardamom seeds, and cumin seeds, combined with ground cinnamon and ground ginger. Featured in Episode 15, planting the rose-petal thread into East Asia. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source.

Name: Dukkah (Egypt)
Short description: Egypt's roasted nut, seed, and spice dip.
Description: Roasted hazelnuts and whole almonds, dry-fried coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and sesame seeds, ground together with a pinch of salt. Served with olive oil and bread. Featured in Episode 16, the direct link back to the Maghreb. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities and timings from the source. Contains hazelnuts, almonds, and sesame.

Name: Hawaij (Arabian Peninsula)
Short description: The Arabian Peninsula's cumin-forward stew spice.
Description: Ground black peppercorns, cumin seeds, cardamom seeds, and coriander seeds, combined with ground turmeric. Used in slow-cooked meats and soups. Featured in Episode 17, closing the Middle East sub-arc. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source. A separate sweet variant swaps the pepper and cumin for ginger, cloves, cinnamon, and fennel.

Name: Garam Masala (North India)
Short description: North India's real garam masala, nothing like supermarket curry powder.
Description: Ground black cardamom seeds, cassia, black peppercorns, black cumin seeds, mace, cloves, and nutmeg, sieved to a fine powder. Stirred in as a finishing spice for dhals, kebabs, biryani, or curries. Featured in Episode 18, opening the South Asia sub-arc. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source. Black cumin and mace can be hard to source outside specialist shops.

Name: Timur ko Chhop (Himalayan Belt)
Short description: The Himalayan Belt's tingling timur-and-chilli table spice.
Description: Dry-roasted timur (or Sichuan pepper as a substitute), mixed with red chilli powder and salt, then ground to a powder. Featured in Episode 19. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source. Timur itself may be hard to source outside Nepali/Himalayan grocers.

Name: Chaat Masala (Central India)
Short description: Central India's tangy, sulphurous street-food seasoning.
Description: Dry-roasted cumin seeds, coriander seeds, and black peppercorns, ground and mixed with amchoor (dried mango powder), ground ginger, asafoetida, kala namak (Himalayan black salt), and salt. Sprinkled over fruit, snacks, and yoghurt. Featured in Episode 20. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source. Kala namak has a distinctive sulphurous smell, worth a heads-up for customers unfamiliar with it.

Name: Panch Phoran (East India & Bangladesh)
Short description: Bengal's five-seed tempering spice, no grinding required.
Description: Cumin seeds, brown mustard seeds, fennel seeds, nigella seeds, and fenugreek seeds, simply combined whole. Fried in oil or ghee at the start of cooking, or used to temper a dish just before serving. Featured in Episode 21. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source, one of the simplest blends in the whole range. Contains mustard.

Name: Vindaloo Paste (West India)
Short description: Goa's Portuguese-rooted vindaloo paste.
Description: Toasted cumin seeds, whole dried Kashmiri chillies, black peppercorns, black mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, cloves, cardamom seeds, cassia, and star anise, ground and mixed with cider or palm vinegar, salt, and jaggery into a stiff paste. Featured in Episode 22. WET, needs adaptation: a vinegar-based paste, not a dry blend; sold as a refrigerated jarred paste, not a shelf-stable dry mix. Contains mustard.

Name: Gunpowder / Podi (South India & Sri Lanka)
Short description: South India's condiment powder for dosa and idli.
Description: Dry-roasted chana dal and urad dal, toasted coconut, black sesame seeds, curry leaves, and red chillies, with tamarind pulp, asafoetida, and jaggery stirred in, ground to a coarse powder. Sprinkled over rice, dosa, or idli, or mixed with oil as a dip. Featured in Episode 23, closing the South Asia sub-arc. Dry-ground condiment, exact quantities from the source; contains tamarind pulp and jaggery, so treat as a semi-moist powder with a shorter shelf life than a pure dry spice mix. Contains sesame.

Name: Yangnyeomjang (South Korea)
Short description: Korea's toasted-sesame-and-gochugaru dipping sauce.
Description: Dry-roasted sesame seeds mixed with soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, rice vinegar, gochugaru (chilli flakes), sugar or honey, crushed garlic, and sliced spring onion. Used as a dip, sauce, and marinade, classically for mandu dumplings. Featured in Episode 24, opening the East Asia sub-arc. WET, needs adaptation: a soy-based sauce, not a dry blend; sold refrigerated, not as a pantry jar. Contains soy and sesame.
Tags: South Korea,Yangnyeomjang,Wet - Needs Adaptation,Contains Soy,Contains Sesame

Name: Shichimi-Togarashi (Japan)
Short description: Japan's seven-spice table condiment.
Description: Finely ground sanshō (or Sichuan pepper), dried orange, yuzu, or lemon peel, chilli powder, nori seaweed flakes, black sesame seeds, hemp, flax, or chia seeds, and garlic powder. Sprinkled over grilled meats, noodles, and curries. Featured in Episode 25. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source. Contains sesame.

Name: Shandong Spice Bag (North China)
Short description: North China's whole-spice infusion bag for master-stock chicken.
Description: Cardamom pods, star anise, whole Sichuan pepper, cloves, ground cumin, a cinnamon stick, liquorice root, and dried orange or tangerine peel, tied in a muslin bag and simmered in stock. Featured in Episode 26. Dry whole-spice sachet, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source.

Name: Nanjing Spice Bag (East China)
Short description: East China's spice bag behind Nanjing's famous salted duck.
Description: Cloves, star anise, crushed whole white pepper, bay leaves, dried tangerine peel, liquorice root powder, and salt, tied in a muslin bag and simmered with fresh ginger and Shaoxing wine. Featured in Episode 27. Dry whole-spice sachet, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source. Fresh ginger and wine are added separately by the cook, not part of the packaged bag.

Name: Five-Spice Powder (South China)
Short description: The classic Cantonese five-spice powder, genuinely better homemade.
Description: Ground star anise, fennel seeds, cloves, a cinnamon stick, and whole Sichuan pepper. Used as a rub for roasting meats or stirred into stir-fries and stews, the defining flavour of Taiwanese lu rou fan. Featured in Episode 28. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source.

Name: Chilli Black Bean Sauce (West China)
Short description: Sichuan's homemade doubanjiang, built for mapo tofu.
Description: Fried bird's eye chillies and fermented black beans, simmered with rice wine, dark rice vinegar, sugar, garlic, and ginger until the oil separates. A homemade version of doubanjiang. Featured in Episode 29, closing the East Asia sub-arc. WET, needs adaptation: a fermented sauce, not a dry blend; sold refrigerated with a limited shelf life (the source notes up to 3 weeks), not as a pantry jar. Contains soy (fermented black beans).

Name: Mole Mix (Mexico & Central America)
Short description: The three-chilli spice mix behind Mexican mole, before it becomes a sauce.
Description: Toasted dried ancho, pasilla, and mulato chillies, ground with cacao nibs, sesame seeds, a cinnamon stick, cumin seeds, anise seeds, black peppercorns, cloves, dried thyme, marjoram, and a bay leaf. Stirred into fried onions, garlic, and tomatoes to make a mole sauce at home. Featured in Episode 30, continuing the Americas sub-arc. Dry blend as packaged, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source, though it's designed to be simmered into a wet sauce by the customer. Contains sesame.

Name: Chimichurri (The Andes)
Short description: Argentina's classic herb-and-oil sauce for grilled steak.
Description: Chilli powder, dried chilli flakes, paprika, finely chopped garlic and onion, parsley or coriander, oregano, wine vinegar, and olive oil, seasoned with salt and black pepper. Served with steak and sausages. Featured in Episode 31. WET, needs adaptation: a fresh oil-and-vinegar sauce with a short shelf life, sold refrigerated rather than as a pantry jar.

Name: Tucupí (Amazon Basin)
Short description: The Amazon's fermented cassava sauce behind pato no tucupí.
Description: Fermented cassava root juice, simmered with garlic, hot red chillies, and black pepper. Served as a broth-like sauce with duck, pork, or fish. Featured in Episode 32. WET, needs adaptation: a fermented liquid sauce with a 24-hour fermentation step, not a dry blend; sold refrigerated with a limited shelf life. Requires careful cassava processing to remove naturally occurring toxins before sale, confirm with a food-safety officer before listing.

Name: BBQ Rub (North America)
Short description: A Kansas-City-meets-Memphis dry rub for steak, brisket, and pulled pork.
Description: Ground cumin, cayenne pepper, chilli powder, brown sugar, black pepper, smoked paprika, onion powder, sea salt, and garlic powder. Rubbed generously onto meat before smoking or slow-cooking. Featured in Episode 33. Dry blend, shelf-stable, exact quantities from the source.

Name: Leche de Tigre (Pacific South America)
Short description: Peru's citrus-chilli ceviche marinade.
Description: Finely chopped ají limo (or habanero), crushed garlic, grated ginger, chopped fresh coriander stalks, finely chopped red onion, and fresh lime juice, seasoned with salt. Used to marinate fish for ceviche, then traditionally drunk on its own afterward. Featured in Episode 34, closing the Americas sub-arc and Season 1. WET, needs adaptation: a fresh citrus marinade with a very short shelf life, sold fresh/refrigerated rather than as a pantry jar.
